instagram.author: shanarra_goode
instagram.body:
Not all AI tools are built the same, and using the wrong one as a solo founder is just as expensive as using none at all.

After a year of testing, building an app from scratch, and running every part of my business alone, I’ve got a very clear picture of what’s actually worth paying for and what’s just noise dressed up as innovation.

The tools that make the GREAT list aren’t there because they’re the most popular. They’re there because they actually do things, not just answer questions, but act, build, automate, and run in the background while I focus on what matters.
The ranking is in the video. 
Disagree with me in the comments, I genuinely want to know what’s in your stack.

#aitools #aiforbusiness #buildinpublic #claudeai #creatorbusiness

instagram.author: samalytics
instagram.body:
Everyone’s talking about AI note-taking apps… but most people are using them wrong.

Here are the 4 I actually think are worth your time; and how to use them to save hours every week.

If you’re still taking notes manually in 2026, you’re already behind.

Comment “SKOOL” and I’ll send you a link to my SKOOL community. 

#ai #techtrends #artificialintelligence
I've tried basically every AI note taking app so you don't have to. These are the only three that are actually worth paying attention to. Number one is Fireflies. If you're working with a team and need your notes to flow directly into tools like Slack, your CRM or Notion, this is a solid choice. It records your meetings, transcribes them and automatically syncs everything to the platforms your team already uses. Number two is Fathom. Perfect if you're a freelancer or working solo, it's completely free with no usage limits, and now it doesn't even show up as a bot in your meetings. It just runs quietly in the background, then sends you a clean summary afterward with clear action items. Number three is TL;DV, you're running a company or managing a team, this is the one I'd go with. You get unlimited recordings, transcripts, and AI summaries for Zoom and team, can even join a meeting on your behalf and after give you a full recap, which is honestly a game changer. Most people spend around 30 plus hours a month in meetings and forget a huge portion of it within a day. These tools fix that. Comment school, and I'll send you a link to my school community where I'm teaching all things AI.

instagram.author: growwithsaransh
instagram.body:
One thing the AI industry is getting very good at?

Convincing people they need the highest plan available.

But after testing most of these tools regularly, I’ve realised the real question isn’t “Which plan is the most powerful?” It’s “Which one actually matches your workflow?”

For most people, the answer is far simpler, and cheaper, than they think.

So I broke down which AI subscriptions I think are genuinely worth paying for right now, and which ones feel unnecessary unless your usage is extremely heavy.

Curious where people disagree.

#reels #aitools #founderlife #foryou #trending

instagram.author: rochelleceballos
instagram.body:
Drop a 💯 if you upgraded from the free version of AI and immediately noticed the difference 😂

Not gonna lie… the free version of AI almost had us giving up too.

It gave us a LITTLE taste of what AI could do…
but it still felt clunky, repetitive, and honestly kinda frustrating at times.

Then we upgraded.

And THAT’S when it started feeling less like a toy…
and more like an actual business tool.

It started remembering things.
Helping organize ideas.
Writing better.
Brainstorming faster.
Helping with content, emails, workflows, planning, customer communication, events… all of it.

If you’re a business owner, I genuinely think it’s worth paying for at least ONE AI platform.

Whichever one you naturally use the most:

- ChatGPT
- Claude
- Gemini

Upgrade it.

The paid versions are where these tools really start becoming useful for busy business owners wearing a million hats.

And honestly…
$20/month to save HOURS every week?
Worth it 😂

Welcome back to HIDDEN GEMS OF THE APP STORE SEASON 4!! 📱💎 This season is all about a curation of apps that make your phone feel fresh, more convenient, and most importantly… FUN TO USE! To kick things off we have a wonderful app called “Albo: Save & Organize” As always, Hidden Gems is a series focused on finding the best apps possible that you may have never heard of, and sometimes these apps offer in-app-subscriptions. Everything shown in this video was captured using the free version of the app, but if you enjoy the experience support for the developer is always worth considering You can find this app in my biosite and keep an eye out for episode 2! 😊💎 #apple #bestapps #hiddengems #appstore #techtok
Welcome to Hidden Gems of the App Store Season 4, part 1. This year we're bringing a brand new curation of apps that will upgrade your phone to feel more fresh, convenient and fun to use. So the first app of this season is called Albo Save and organized. Instead of endlessly bookmarking things into the void that you'll never go back to, Albo is a centralized space to save things you come across in any app and helps you actually do the things that you. Let's say for example, you save a real or a TikTok on a recipe you want to try. The app analyzes the content and then populates step by step instructions with an ingredient list based on what was in the original post. Or maybe you're going on a trip. I'm going to Japan later this year, so I saved a potential hotel I'm interested in. And not only does the app find details on the location based on the post you saved, but it can also show you other content that also features this same location. It even populates a map of all the location based stuff that you save. So if you're planning a trip of your own or just looking for places you want to visit, again, it's all right there and super easy to find. I love this feature. And as always, the series is never sponsored and only features apps that I have personally tested myself. So comment Hidden Gems Below if you want me to send you a direct link to this one and consider following or subscribing if you want to see Part 2.
